camera.position: on the boards, fixed, wide shot of most of the rink

events.cues: left-to-right travel, alternating pushes, moderate knee bend, upright posture, arms low and close to the body rather than extended
events.note: readable at 15 fps; skater ~40% of frame height here — the closest pass in the clip

observations: Whole-rink framing: for most of the 138 s the skater is 5-15% of frame height — too small for pose analysis.
People walk between camera and ice at 7.5s, 37s, 75s and 113s, fully blocking the view.
Several skaters share the ice; a tracker would need to lock onto the subject (white tee, cap, dark shorts).
No jumps or spins occur in this clip — nothing to detect beyond skating and gliding.
120 fps survived AirDrop intact; motion blur is low and frames are sharp even on the close passes.
verdict: Good camera settings, wrong framing. Usable as a negative/landscape example, not as a skill example.
